standard_prerequisites.name: Limit preserving behaviour of the flatness functor at primes, and the finite presentation argument from the local flattening theorem

standard_prerequisites.use: The first shows the functor is limit preserving when the sources and the module are of finite presentation, and the second supplies the argument giving finite presentation of the closed subscheme.

core_obligations: Cut out the locus by an intersection: for each point of the closed fibre take the closed subscheme of the base produced by the scheme theoretic flattening statement, and note that the intersection over the given subset satisfies the required equivalence (proof lines 6948-6951).

Reduce to the affine case for the last statement: under the finite presentation assumptions choose finitely many affine opens covering the given closed quasi-compact subset, so that it suffices to treat each of them, hence one may assume the source affine (proof lines 6953-6959).

Conclude finite presentation: in the affine case the functor defined by the flatness condition is limit preserving, so the argument from the local flattening theorem shows that the closed subscheme is of finite presentation (proof lines 6960-6965).
proof_roadmap: Intersection of the pointwise flattening subschemes (proof lines 6948-6951).
Reduction to the affine case over a finite cover (proof lines 6953-6959).
Finite presentation of the subscheme via the limit preserving argument (proof lines 6960-6965).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a closed subscheme of a henselian local base over which flatness of the module along the fibre at all points of a given subset of the closed fibre is exactly tested, with finite presentation of that subscheme under finite presentation hypotheses and closed quasi-compactness of the subset (statement lines 6930-6946, tag 05PG-adjacent). The first part is an intersection of the pointwise flattening subschemes; the second reduces to the affine case over a finite affine cover of the subset and then applies a limit preserving argument to conclude finite presentation. The reduction and the limit preserving step are the substance, so the claim is H2.
